speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) why does NEA require stallholders to personally operate their hawker stalls; (b) how is this aligned with the objectives of hawker centres; and (c) whether there are any circumstances where NEA exercises flexibility when hawker stallholders are temporarily unable to operate their stalls due to personal reasons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: If this requirement is not imposed, the tenant who has successfully bid for the stall could potentially sublet the stall and collect the difference in rent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It may encourage persons to bid for a stall without an intention to run a stall but only to sublet it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: If the tenant is unable to operate the stall, he is expected to return the stall to NEA which will then release the stall for other interested hawkers to bid for the stall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This will give new hawkers a fair chance to enter the trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The Member asks whether there are any circumstances where NEA exercises flexibility when hawker stallholders are temporarily unable to operate their stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA supports hawkers who wish to expand their businesses by allowing individuals to hold up to two cooked food stalls in our hawker centres, provided they are able to divide their time and operate the stalls personally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Hawkers have also made use of other arrangements to grow their businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Some take on more stalls at hawker centres with their family members as stallholders or sell their recipes to other hawkers who in turn successfully bid for those stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Others continue to operate their stalls personally even as they expand their businesses to other establishments, such as coffee shops and food courts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For those who are unable to personally operate their hawker stalls, they may relinquish their stalls or hand them over to a family member.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: There are also hawkers who enter into franchise arrangements, where they can leverage established brands to start or grow their businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This is a good way for them to learn the ropes and enter the food and beverage (F&B) space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It is in this context that we sometimes see stalls carrying the same brand across different hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA does not restrict such arrangements, as long as registered stallholders in hawker centres are still able to fulfil the tenancy requirements by personally operating their stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA generally does not allow corporates to bid directly for and operate hawker stalls as this could crowd out aspiring hawkers, and run counter to our intent of providing opportunities for Singaporeans to run small food businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We have made some exceptions based on social considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: For example, operators of Socially-conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres are allowed to run a small number of stalls as part of their operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: But these operators are required to plough back at least 50% of any surpluses to benefit the centre and stallholders, such as by providing shuttle services from transport nodes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Our hawker centres have played an integral role in nation building and hawker culture has been an important part of the Singapore identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We want our hawker centres to continue providing opportunities for Singaporeans to directly operate their own small food businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will continue to support them as best as we can.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: First of all, does the current rule of requiring hawkers to personally operate the stall have actually been effective in preventing unintended subletting and has it also unintentionally discouraged genuine hawkers?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In the case of hawkers who are intending to expand, can they re-assign their stall leases to business partner without the need to re-bid or to re-apply for their stalls?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second clarification is that, today, for new hawkers to grow their business, they actually have to invest in branding, work on social media marketing and some might also set up their central kitchen or choose shared services.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And many of these business activities require them to be physically present elsewhere than physically present at their stalls.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My understanding is that today, for a stallholder, they must actually operate minimally eight hours physically.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Or in the case where they have two stalls, they have to be physically present at the stall for four hours.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can the Ministry exercise some flexibilities for hawkers who may need to be outside of the stall because there are many other business activities that they have to operate?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On his first question about personally operating the stall, we believe that physical presence is actually the most practical and fair way of ensuring that the stall is not sublet and the person is operating it personally.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because through these inspections, NEA is able to directly monitor whether stallholders physically operate their stalls during the stall's operating hours.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The truth is, to catch subletting is not so easy, because it is a private arrangement that can take place between the person who has bid for the place but has no intention to run it and under the table, could be collecting subletting income from someone else and profiting from rent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: What we do not want is for a subletter to then profit from the huge margin by extracting rent from the person who is interested to run the stall and pass the cost subsequently to consumers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And if there is a way for us to catch it better, we would want that.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, if there are suspicions of subletting, NEA would follow up on feedback where possible.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Nonetheless, NEA also understands that there are some stallholders who may need to be away from their stalls for a short period of time, to run quick errands for example.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In such cases, we will exercise flexibility and give these stallholders the ability to do so without taking any penalty actions on them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But to nominate the stall to an unrelated person opens up the risk of someone then profiteering and buying whatever has been given to this person through a business transaction.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is something that we will not allow.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The Senior Minister of State said that you will exercise flexibility – I had a resident, for instance, who had sought that flexibility by asking for a window by which he had to physically be present at the stall for the inspections.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand again, of course, that you want there to be some kind of spot checks to prevent instances of subletting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But nevertheless, it seems like giving a window is a reasonable accommodation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Is that not something that is considered part of that flexibility?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But there are place managers at each and every one of our hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I do hope that there is communication between the place manager and the hawker who may need some flexibility on the ground to do so.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I believe our principle is to make sure that we allow flexibility where it is needed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But if it is time and again when the things are flouted and it is too much of a repeat ask, then I think it calls into question whether that is a genuine need or whether there are some actions to try and circumvent our rules.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we have to take things on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I would say that, in the end, it really is about what we want to see our hawker culture thrive.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There are many successful hawkers who have done well and expanded their business outside of hawker centres, but yet they try their very best to run those one or two stalls that they started their business with personally.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But there are also those who have successfully branched out to other F&B establishments where there are no restrictions like what we have, and they have chosen to give up their hawker stalls as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I think to be fair to all players, we have to respect the rules.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: I think the Senior Minister of State answered my first clarification.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: On my second clarification, where I shared that today, many of the new hawkers are also investing in time on social media marketing, they could be at the central kitchen preparing some of the ingredients, they could be doing deliveries to their customers – and they cannot be physically at the stall.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: But today, some of the place managers are actively enforcing, based on strict hours, for example, eight hours if they have one stall; four hours, they have two stalls.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: Will there be flexibility accorded in terms of the actual hours they are physically present?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: And how will this flexibility be consistent and fair throughout all NEA hawker centres?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because as I said in my earlier reply to the Member Jamus Lim, if a hawker's business has grown to a size where they are unable to split the time properly and they have to focus their time more on the businesses outside the hawker centres, then I think it is time for them to really take a hard look and see where their main revenue source is coming from.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think if they have grown to such a scale, they ought to focus on that and they may have to give up that stall in which we are giving them, to some extent, a lower rent and a lower barrier to entry, to someone else who may need the space more.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I know there are members of the public who have seen this particular case that has surfaced on the Internet recently, on social media.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think the Member Mr Chia has engaged this particular hawker before, Mr Noorman Mubarak.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: He put up a social media post about his wife who's pregnant and is unable to run the stall personally.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are quite happy that hawkers like him have succeeded, but it is understandable that as a business owner he wants to focus on his other business and try not to focus as much attention on the hawker stalls.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But that is not something that we would want, because we cannot allow our NEA hawker system to be catering to the interest of such private chain owners.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We need to make sure that there are opportunities for others to enter the trade as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Let us remember that hawker centres are not just commercial spaces, but they are also community dining spaces with a social role.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We have invested in our hawker centres to provide affordable cooked food for Singaporeans, while wanting to enable small food businesses to earn a reasonable living.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we have deliberately kept the barrier to entry low to allow many hawkers, including like Mr Mubarak himself, to build a successful business and expand to other F&B establishment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, if we did not enforce these rules, what would the alternative be?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Should we allow stalls to be fully run by hired workers as businesses expand and they cannot run the stalls themselves?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If so, hawker centres would become rather indistinguishable from coffee shops and food courts, eroding the authenticity.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And over time, our hawker culture will be diluted, shifting from passionate hawkers serving their own dishes to our customers, to businesses just prioritising efficiency and scale over heritage and quality.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We support technology adoption, be it central kitchen, be it marketing technology through social media to improve.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But what we want is to make sure that as they do so, they do not compromise and erode the culture that we are trying to protect and grow.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, while we support technology to improve stall level efficiency, we should not do so at the expense of our hawkers stepping away from running the stalls themselves and letting the workers just take over the day-to-day running and cooking of the food.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The reality, therefore, is that we need to balance between protecting our heritage, keeping the food affordable and ensuring fair opportunities for new hawkers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, these are quite difficult to maintain if we do not have rules to manage.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It would have been far easier for NEA to let the hawker centres just operate like any other commercial outfits, such as food courts or coffee shops, without any restrictions on subletting or any business model that the operators wish to do.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But that would mean losing what makes them really special today.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, if Singaporeans are prepared to accept hawker food at price points, quality and the business model just like any other coffee shops or food courts, then we could remove these restrictions and let the free market take its course.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But for now, we believe these regulations will help ensure that hawker centres remain a place for authentic, accessible and culturally significant food experiences for Singaporeans.
